topic: Safe light in a blackout: torches and headlamps instead of candles

slides.title: *1 torch* per person. Zero candles.
slides.body: Safe light for a blackout, without the fire risk.

slides.title: Headlamp *first*
slides.body: Hands stay free on stairs and at the stove. Keep one by each bed.

slides.title: Spare *batteries*
slides.body: Store them next to the light. Add one battery lantern for the table.

content.caption:
1 torch per person. Zero candles. That's the simple rule for safe blackout light.

Torches and headlamps don't need a flame, so there's no open fire near curtains, pets or sleeping people.

- A headlamp keeps your hands free on stairs and in the kitchen.
- Keep one light by each bed, so you're not feeling around in the dark.
- Store spare batteries next to the lights, and check them twice a year.
- A battery lantern on the table lights the whole room.

If you do use a candle, use a stable holder and never leave it alone. Better still, skip it.
